findings.evidence: The diff adds `athena-core --test automation_register 5.00`. crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs `missing_timing_lines` reports any --test unit that has no line in xtask/shard-timings.txt, so without this line the repo checks would fail. Earlier spec-mechanism changes (OLY-B-A3-02, OLY-B-A4-04) did the same, and the CHANGELOG entry discloses it.

summary: The change passes. It adds an automation register in crates/athena-core/src/automation.rs and exports it from lib.rs. Each entry records its owner, cost, measured savings and the toil or repeat cause it came from. `register` refuses an entry that has no savings, no owner or no source. `review` lists the entries that cost more than they save for retirement, and separately lists the entries with no savings. docs/spec.toml now names this module and its test as the mechanism of OLY-B-A9-01; the owner stays Athena, and the measure names the test command and ends with `status: not shown`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --test automation_register` and all 6 tests passed. They cover the retire, keep and refuse outcomes, and they check the real spec entry, so a mechanism of "none" would fail them. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI checks on this tree. The approach is sound: cost and savings are measured in the same unit over the same period, and the rule only retires when cost is strictly higher. The one finding is minor: xtask/shard-timings.txt is not on the deliverables list, but the repository's mirror check requires a line for every new test file.
